# Crosswalk: digital twins, synthetic data and the behavioral panel

> Crosswalk is an opted-in consumer panel of 30 million people worldwide, 10 million of them in the US. It reads what audiences actually do across their entire digital life, and Digital Twins IQ builds a digital twin of each US panelist from observed behavior.

This file carries the full text of the pages listed in https://www.crosswalknyc.com/llms.txt that explain Crosswalk's digital twins, synthetic data and behavioral panel. Every page is also live at the address above each section.


---

<!-- https://www.crosswalknyc.com/digital-twins.html -->

# Digital twins built from what ten million people actually do.

A digital twin is a working copy of a real person's behavior. Digital Twins IQ (Twin IQ for short) builds one for each of the 10 million US people in the Crosswalk panel, which counts 30 million people worldwide. It comes from what they watch, search, buy, and pay for, not from what they tell a survey. Put a plan, a title, a price, or an idea in front of the twins and see what happens before you spend.

Synthetic data, grounded in real behavior. Clients see group statistics only. No individual is ever identified.

## Digital Twins IQ lets you test your spend on ten million real lives.

Every person in the Crosswalk panel gets a twin built from what they do. You put in a plan, a title, or an idea. Prometheus runs it forward on the twins and returns the odds, the audience, and the package that earns the most. Then it sets the plan live inside the ad platforms and keeps score.

_How Crosswalk digital twins work, in under five minutes: the panel, the twin, the forecast, and the record on Election 2026 and the NCIS: New York pilot._
One twin per person: observed behavior, 4,600+ audiences already read, outside anchors, and what each person pays.

Twin and AI research tools raised more than $250 million in the past year. Every one of them is built on what people say, none on what they do.

The only panel that sees each person's whole digital life, joined to products that already read live campaigns.

## Synthetic data that starts with real data.

Most synthetic data starts with a survey, or with a language model guessing how a type of person would answer. Crosswalk's digital twins start with the record: a real person's digital life over time, kept in order with timing. The twin learns how that person responds, what they pay, and when they leave. The synthetic part is what you do with it. Run a plan the person never saw and read how people like them respond.

**Digital twin**
One real person's observed behavior, turned into a copy that can respond to something new.

**Synthetic data**
The outcomes the twins produce when you run a plan they have never seen. New data, built on real behavior.

**Synthetic audience**
The twins a plan would reach, sized, described, and projected to the US population.

**Not a survey**
No twin here was built from a questionnaire, an interview, or a model guessing at a type of person.

## What one twin carries.

Four layers of fact and two of judgment, for each of ten million people.

### Observed behavior.

This person's watching, searching, buying, paying, and clicking, kept as a sequence with timing, across every surface.

### The corpus.

Everything already read about people like them: 4,600+ audiences, every journey, every attribution, churn, and trend read.

### Outside anchors.

Public facts the panel cannot see, fixed on as anchors: box office and streaming history, platform reach, ad benchmarks, prices paid.

### Response and price.

Past responses to content and ads, how long each took, the prices this person paid, and the ones they walked away from.

### Lifecycle.

Their standing with each title, platform, or brand: discovering, trying, in the habit, lapsing, or coming back.

### A track record.

How well twins like this one forecast the campaigns in the corpus, published next to every new read.

## Four steps from the plan to the result.

Put it in, run it forward, make it better, set it live and prove it.

### Put it in.

A plan, a budget, assets, a trailer, a script, a logline, a creator roster, or a price, typed to Prometheus or attached as a file.

### Run it forward.

The twins the plan can reach respond the way people like them did before. Thousands of runs become odds and ranges.

### Make it better.

Prometheus works every lever and ranks them by what they earn, then returns the package that reaches the goal for less money.

### Set it live.

Approve it, and it runs inside the ad platforms, moves money toward rising signal, tests, and keeps the ledger of what it saved.

_Step one, as a screen. You describe the plan the way you would say it. Prometheus reads it back as fields you can edit, then runs it on the twins._

## Launch Lab.

A plan run on the twins before the money goes out. For studios, streamers, labels, and game publishers with a release to open.

- Three plans side by side: as allocated, signal-led, and the minimum that still hits the goal
- Odds and ranges on the goal, week by week
- The levers ranked by what they earn
- A holdout sized to prove lift at the lowest spend
The signal-led plan sells 23% more opening-weekend tickets on the same budget, and the review clips lead instead of the trailer.

_Launch Lab._

## Greenlight Lab.

The odds on a title or a bare idea before money is committed. For development, acquisitions, financing, and slate decisions.

- A logline, script, trailer, roster, or pilot goes in
- The range of outcomes on each platform
- The audience that shows up, sized by cohort
- Levers ranked by value, with one package to run
A seven in ten chance the limited series clears 4M viewers in its first month on Peacock, and the lead carries 71% of the reach.

_Greenlight Lab._

## Spend Engine.

The connected loop that moves money toward what is working. For brands, agencies, and partners with always-on paid media.

- Meta, Google, Amazon, and TikTok connected, read and write
- Daily moves by chip, or on the rule you set
- A/B tests spun from the trends
- Lift read against a matched twin holdout
A $50,000 test on matched twins reads with the confidence of a seven-figure one, and the account moves budget the next morning.

_Spend Engine._

## Four kinds of buyer, one engine.

Each one brings a decision that today gets made on a hunch, a survey, or last year's numbers.

### Studios and streamers.

P&A and launch teams opening a film, a season, an album, or a game. Launch Lab, per release.

### Development and slate.

Greenlight, acquisitions, and financing decisions. Greenlight Lab, per read or per slate.

### Brands and agencies.

Always-on paid social and search. Spend Engine, connected to the platforms they already buy.

### Partners through the API.

Platforms and agencies that build on Crosswalk: reads at rate-card prices, with the savings ledger returned in the API.

Next to the others. Profile IQ tells you who the audience is. Digital Journey IQ shows the path they took. Attribution IQ gives each touchpoint its credit. Digital Twins IQ takes the same people and runs the plan you have not spent on yet.

## A survey-built twin cannot tell you what a dollar will do.

Survey-built twins and synthetic respondents are good at what people say. Spend decisions depend on what people do: whether they click, watch, pay, come back, or leave, and how long each takes. Crosswalk's twins were built from that record, and they are checked against live campaigns.

## Every forecast sits next to what happened.

Before any client sees a forecast, the engine runs on the past. Every campaign and launch in the corpus is replayed from the day before it started, with only what was knowable then, and scored against the result. The score is published inside the product and updated as live campaigns land.

The engine's score on the past campaigns that look most like yours is on the page with the forecast.

The live signal comes in daily. The forecast is re-scored and the plan moves with it.

What was forecast, what happened, and what the twins saved go into a ledger you can open any time.

The public record is here: every call we made before its outcome, dated, scored, the misses included.

## Twins, not people.

Each twin stands in for one of the 10 million US panelists who chose to be counted. Identity is kept apart from behavior, and sensitive details are removed before anything is stored. Prometheus never answers about one person. It answers about the group a person is counted with, and every projected figure carries its base.

## Digital twins and synthetic data, in plain words.

### What is a digital twin in market research?

A digital twin is a copy of a real person's behavior that can respond to something new. In research it stands in for a survey respondent. Crosswalk builds one from observed behavior over time for each of the 10 million US people in its 30 million-person panel. A question about a plan or a title is answered by how people like that behave.

### What does synthetic data based on real data mean?

Synthetic data is data that was produced rather than observed. Crosswalk produces it by running a plan on twins built from real behavior. The inputs are real: what people watched, searched, bought, and paid. The output is new: what those same people would do with a plan they have not seen yet.

### How is this different from a synthetic panel or AI respondents?

Most synthetic panels start from surveys, interviews, or a language model answering as a type of person. They can tell you what people say. Crosswalk's twins start from what people do, and they are checked against live campaigns rather than against another survey.

### How accurate are the digital twins?

Every forecast is scored against what happened, and that score sits next to each new read inside the product. Before any client sees a forecast, the twins are run on past launches and campaigns using only what was knowable at the time.

### What can I test on the twins?

A media plan and its budget split, a title, a script, a trailer, a bare idea, a creator roster, a price or a promotion, a release week, an audience. Anything you would otherwise spend money to find out.

### Does it connect to our ad platforms?

Yes. The recommended plan exports in the shape each platform's buyer uploads from day one. Connected accounts on Meta, Google, Amazon, and TikTok add daily reads and, with your approval, the moves themselves.

### Is any personal data used or sold?

No customer files are sold and no individual is identified. The panel is opted in, identity is kept apart from behavior, and clients receive group statistics projected to the US population.

### How do I start?

Talk to us. Digital Twins IQ opens to Crosswalk clients first, and Prometheus already answers audience questions on the same 10 million people today.

Bring a plan, a script, or a title. We will run it on the twins and walk you through the read. Prometheus answers audience questions on the same ten million people today.

# Every call we make goes on the record before the outcome.

A forecast or a room count that cannot be checked is an opinion. Ours are dated the moment they are made, scored the moment the outcome lands, and kept here for anyone to read, the misses included.

## Three steps, the same for every count.

A call goes on this record before its result exists: the question, the audience, the figure and its range, the day the result is due and what will settle it, with a hash of all of it. A call is never rewritten; a later read is a new, dated row.

Every day the record checks the calls that came due. A certified result, a published figure, or our own count of what the audience did is written next to the call. A call made after its result was knowable is marked and never scored.

How far the figure was off, whether the outcome fell inside the range given, and whether the side we called was the side that won. The misses stay on the page. A scored miss is worth more than a soft number.

## Every count carries a range and one of three words.

The word comes from what the count rests on, how far the room agreed by the people its seats stand for, how steady the count's own range was, how calls like it have scored on this page, and how much was on file about the thing asked. The room always makes the call; the word says how firm it is.

The room is sure of this one. The count rests on something counted, or the record shows calls like it land close. The range is tight.

A lean, not a lock. The count rests on what was found about the thing asked and on how the room answered; the range is wider.

An early call. The room still names who leads and by how much; the range is wide, and it tightens as calls like it settle on this page.

## What we said, what happened.

Every scored call the twins made before its outcome, newest first. Nothing made after the fact is on it.

| Audience | What was asked | We said | What happened | Miss | Called | Settled | Dated by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Loading the record. |

A miss on a count is the share of the figure that happened; a miss on a split is the points that would have to move for the two to match. "On the right side" means the side we called was the side that won.

## Bring us something we can be wrong about.

A premiere, a launch, a price change. We will put the call on this page before it settles.

Source: https://www.crosswalknyc.com/twins-track-record.html

# How Crosswalk's digital twins work.

A digital twin is a copy of an audience that you can ask questions. Crosswalk builds each twin from 5+ years of what 10 million real people did online. Inside every twin are at least 12 archetypes: groups of people who act alike. In a focus group, one person speaks for each group. You ask a question and see how many people would pick each answer, and how sure we are.

Published November 2026 by Crosswalk Technologies, Inc. · Download the full methodology (PDF) · See the public track record

## How it works in four steps

You pick an audience, we build its twin, you ask it something, and you get the answer with the people behind it.

- Pick the audience. The people who watch a show, use a service, follow a star or buy a brand. Or describe a group yourself, such as women 25 to 44 in Dallas.
- We build the twin. We look at what those people did online over the past 5+ years, then find the archetypes inside the audience.
- Ask it something. Ask questions in a focus group, bring one business question, or show it a video.
- Get the answer. You see what share of the audience picked each answer, how many people that is, why they picked it, and how firm the answer is.

## Five words used on this page

**Twin**
A copy of a real audience that you can ask questions.

**Archetype**
A group of people inside the audience who act alike, such as "parents who stopped watching after the season ended."

**Archetype representative**
The one person who speaks for an archetype. Each has a name, an age and a city.

**Focus group**
A room with one seat for each archetype. You ask, and every representative answers.

**How firm**
Every answer comes with one of three words: firm, leaning or early. The word tells you how close the real number should be.

## Why this method is stronger

Most twins are built from what people say in a survey or an interview, or from a chatbot playing a type of person. Ours are built from what people did.

- Real people. 10 million US people stand behind the twins, about 1 in 33 Americans. A typical survey hears from a few thousand.
- Years of history. We have more than 2,000 days of what the same people did. A survey or an interview captures one moment.
- Every screen. Phone, laptop and TV count as one person, so we see the search, the show and the purchase that came after.
- Up to date. New behavior arrives every morning.
- Groups found in the data. The audience decides its own archetypes. Nobody hand-picks personas.
- Answers in real people. Every share comes with the number of US people behind it.
- A public record. We write down each prediction before the result and keep every miss on a public page.

## Where a twin comes from

Every twin starts with real behavior. Crosswalk's panel is 10 million US people who chose to be counted, and we see their whole digital life.

That means what they watch and stream, what they search for, what they buy, and what they sign up for or cancel. We see it on every screen, day by day, since January 2021. A twin is built from that history.

### Three ways to build one

- An audience we already know. The viewers of a show, the fans of a star, the users of a service or the buyers of a brand. If we do not have it yet, we build it first, usually in under an hour.
- A group you describe. Pick gender, age, income, ethnicity and where people live. You can set the shares yourself.
- A list of links. Paste links to a show page, a channel, a feed or an article. The twin is the people who went there.

## Finding the archetypes

We sort the audience into groups of people who act alike. Every twin gets at least 12 groups, and it can have more.

First we sort people by where they are with the subject. There are five stages: just found it, trying it, in the habit, drifting away, and back after a break. Then we sort by age. Very small groups join the group closest to them. If fewer than 12 groups are left, we split the biggest ones, for example by gender or age.

Each archetype gets a plain name and one representative to speak for it. Here are four of the 16 archetypes in the Amazon Prime Video twin, which stands for 128,116,302 US subscribers.

| Archetype | People | Representative |
|---|---|---|
| Older regulars on sport and crime series | 16,572,733 | Devin, 65, Tampa |
| Thursday night football people | 15,200,112 | Caleb, 53, Los Angeles |
| Under-35 fans of The Boys and Fallout | 14,605,258 | Kenji, 33, New York |
| Parents who keep it on for the kids | 3,587,256 | Leah, 45, Seattle |

All 16 archetypes together add up to the full 128,116,302.

## What happens in the focus group

The focus group has one seat for each archetype. Every representative answers in their own words, and each answer counts for the people behind it.

- At least 12 seats. There is one seat per archetype, so the audience sets the number. You never pick it.
- It looks like the audience. If a twin is 72% women, about 9 of 12 seats go to women.
- Bigger groups count more. Devin speaks for 16.6 million people and Leah for 3.6 million. His answer counts about 4.6 times as much as hers.
- Representatives remember. They recall what they said earlier, in this group and in past groups on the same twin, as a real person would.

### When you ask a question

- The focus group first learns the facts about your subject: what it is, when it came out and where it plays.
- Each representative answers in two or three sentences, based on what their group did before. They also say how sure they are, from 1 to 5.
- We add up the people behind each answer.
- You get a short summary, the quotes that explain it, and two questions worth asking next.
Example: one question on the Prime Video twin, November 18, 2026

"Which of these would get you most excited if it finally became a show?"

The answer: 63.1% of subscribers, about 80.8 million people, picked "a game I play." Nine of the 16 seats chose it. Those seats speak for bigger groups, so the share of people is higher than the share of seats.

Kenji, 33, chose the game. "A game I play, no contest, because Fallout did exactly that for me."

Devin, 65, chose a book series. "A game means nothing to me at my age."

## Three words that tell you how sure we are

Every answer comes with a range and one of three words. The word tells you how close the real number should be to ours.

| Word | How close | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Firm | Within about 5 points | We are sure of this one. |
| Leaning | Within about 12 points | A lean, not a lock. |
| Early | Up to about 20 points | The range is wide, but you still get an answer. |

In the example above, the 63.1% was leaning. The real share should fall between 51.2% and 75.0%.

### Our predictions, checked in public

We write down each prediction before the result is known. When the result comes in, we score it. Misses stay on the record.

| What we predicted | We said | What happened | The miss |
|---|---|---|---|
| Texas Senate: who wins | Talarico 54.6%, Paxton 43.3% | Talarico 55.1%, Paxton 43.0% | Right winner; within 0.5 points |
| Nevada 4th District: the margin | By 23.0 points | By 22.7 points | 0.3 points |
| Ohio governor: turnout and winner | 4.2M of 7.9M; the winner | About 4.6M; the winner | 8.7% under; right winner |
| NCIS: New York, week-one audience | 10.04M | 10.25M | 2.0% under |
| NCIS: New York, share who finish the pilot | 83.9% | 81.6% | 2.3 points over |
| NCIS: New York, share back for episode two | 85.7% | 86.8% | 1.1 points under |

That is six predictions scored as of November 17, 2026. All three winners were called right. On average, our numbers were off by 3.2%, about 3 in 100. The full list is on the track record page.

## One business question, answered by Predictive Analytics

Bring one business question. Prometheus, our research assistant, writes 5 to 8 questions, asks them in a focus group, and gives you a verdict with a full report.

Your question can take almost any shape. It might be "Will this win?", "Should we do this?" or "What will people pay?" The plan starts wide, with where the audience stands today. Then it narrows to what pulls people in and what holds them back. Last comes your question itself. Planning is free, and you can edit or drop any question first.

Example: the Prime Video run, November 18, 2026

The question: which new show or sport, found on no other service, would get people to pay for Prime Video? The verdict: a new weeknight live sports package. 55.7% of subscribers, about 71.3 million people, picked it. That is about 4 times the 14.1% who said nothing would get them to pay.

## Pilot Testing for shows and ads

Pilot Testing shows your video to the focus group. Each representative watches it, reacts, answers questions, and fills out a scorecard at the end.

- Add your video. A pilot, an episode, an ad or a film, from 15 seconds to 4 hours. Upload it or paste a link.
- We learn who is on screen. Faces are matched to your cast list. Only people on your list are ever named.
- Each representative turns a dial. The dial runs from 0 to 100 and moves as they watch, with a reading every 2 to 4 seconds. A 43-minute pilot gets 706 readings per representative.
- You can ask questions as it plays. Questions come at the turns of the story, and you can add your own at any moment.
- A scorecard comes at the end. It asks what studios ask after a screening: the rating, and whether people would recommend it, finish it and come back for the next episode.
- Then a forecast. How many people would watch in week one, how many would finish the season, and how many would sign up to watch it.
After the test you can play the dial back to any second and see what was on screen and what people said. A test screening needs a recruiter, a room and a week. Pilot Testing needs the file.

## What you get

Every result comes back as files you can share: a CSV, a PDF and, for twins and Pilot Testing, a deck.

When you finish a focus group, Prometheus also emails you a PDF of the session with a link back to it.

## Privacy

Everyone on the panel chose to be counted and can leave at any time. We never answer about one person, only about groups.

Identity is kept apart from behavior. Clients see group results scaled up to the US population. Read how the panel works and the Privacy Policy.

More detail. Every step and figure is in the full methodology PDF.

## The methodology, in plain words.

### What is a Crosswalk digital twin built from?

From what real people did. Crosswalk sees the whole digital life of 10 million US people who chose to be counted, day by day since January 2021. No surveys, no interviews, and no chatbot guessing at a type of person.

### How many archetypes does a twin have?

At least 12, and there can be more. The audience decides the number. If an audience has fewer than 12 clear groups, we split the biggest ones until there are 12.

### Why does one answer count more than another?

Representatives speak for groups of different sizes. One may speak for 16.6 million people and another for 3.6 million. The bigger group's answer counts for more, so the result matches the real audience.

### What do firm, leaning and early mean?

They tell you how close the real number should be. Firm means within about 5 points. Leaning means within about 12. Early means a wider range, up to about 20 points.

### How accurate are Crosswalk's digital twins?

We publish every prediction before the result and score it after. On the first six, all three winners were called right, and our numbers were off by 3.2% on average.

### Do the answers change over time?

They can, because people change. A twin keeps learning from what its people do, so a question asked next month may get a different answer. The answer follows the audience.

### What can Pilot Testing watch?

A pilot, an episode, an ad, a film or a run of episodes, from 15 seconds to 4 hours. Upload an MP4, MOV, WebM or M4V file, or paste a link.

### Is any person identified?

No. We only answer about groups, never about one person. Identity is kept apart from behavior, and clients see group results scaled up to the US population.

Source: https://www.crosswalknyc.com/digital-twins-methodology.html

# What is a digital twin audience?

A digital twin audience is a working copy of a real group of people that you can ask questions. The strongest twins are built from what people did, not what they told a survey. Crosswalk builds every twin from 5+ years of behavior on 10 million opted-in US people, about 1 in 33 Americans. Ask it about a show, a price, a plan or a launch. It tells you what the audience will most likely do, and how firm that answer is.

Updated November 2026 · Crosswalk Technologies, Inc. · Read the full methodology

## The short definition

A digital twin, in engineering, is a live digital copy of a machine. In audience research, a digital twin is a live digital copy of a group of people. You can test something on the twin before you spend money on the real audience.

The idea is simple. If you know what a group of people did for five years, you can ask what they would do next. A twin stores that history and answers from it. The answer is not a guess from a chatbot. It is a read of how people like that have behaved before.

## A twin is not one average person

A real audience is made of different groups. A Crosswalk twin keeps those groups apart. Each group is an archetype, and each archetype has one person who speaks for it.

Take the people who subscribe to Amazon Prime Video in the US: 128,116,302 of them. Inside that audience are 16 archetypes. The biggest is older regulars who watch sport and crime series, about 1 in 8 of the audience. Another is under-35 fans of The Boys and Fallout, about 1 in 9. A smaller one is parents who stopped watching after the season ended, about 1 in 18. Each archetype gets a plain name and a person to stand for it, such as Devin, 65, from Tampa.

When you ask the twin a question, every archetype answers. Then the count adds up the real people behind each answer. An archetype of 16.6 million people counts for more than one of 3.6 million. That is why a twin can give you a percentage and a people count, not just a mood.

## What a digital twin is built from

There are three ways a vendor can build a digital twin. The method decides what the twin can tell you.

| Built from | What it misses |
|---|---|
| Surveys and interviews | What people do when nobody is asking. People misremember and overstate. |
| A language model playing a type of person | It has never met the audience. It repeats the average of the internet. |
| Observed behavior over time | Private feelings that never show up in behavior |

Crosswalk twins are the third kind. Every twin is built from the record of what 10 million opted-in US people did across their entire digital life. That record holds what they watched and streamed, what they searched, what they bought, what they paid for and what they cancelled. It runs day by day since January 2021. Each person is one ID across their phone, laptop and TV.

For the full build, including the twelve habits every twin carries and the five stages a person moves through, read the Digital Twins IQ methodology.

## Why Crosswalk's digital twins are better

A twin can only be as good as what it is built from. Crosswalk builds from a record few companies hold: years of what the same real people did, on every screen.

- Real lives behind every answer. The panel holds 10 million opted-in US people. A big survey reaches a few thousand, and a chatbot persona reaches no one.
- Years of history. Each person's record runs day by day since January 2021. An interview-built twin knows one conversation.
- The whole day, on every screen. Search, streaming, social, shopping, apps and gaming are joined under one ID across phone, laptop and TV. A platform's own data sees only its own app.
- Fresh every morning. Yesterday's behavior is in today's twin. A chatbot knows the world as of its training.
- Counts in people, not just percentages. Each answer carries the number of real US people behind it, so you can plan with it.
- One business question, a full plan. Predictive Analytics writes 5 to 8 questions from wide to narrow, runs them, and hands back a verdict with a report.
- A public record. Every call goes on the record before the result and is scored when it lands. On the first six, three winners were called right.

## What you can ask a digital twin

Anything you would ask the real audience, and some things you could not. You can also put a video in front of it and watch how it reacts.

- A focus group question. "Which of these would you pay for?" The room answers, seat by seat, and the count adds up the people. See how an AI focus group works.
- A business question. "If we raise the price $2, how many people leave?" Predictive Analytics plans 5 to 8 questions from wide to narrow. It runs the room and hands back a verdict with a report.
- A cut of a show or an ad. Pilot Testing seats the room in front of your video. Each seat turns a dial from 0 to 100 as it watches, and fills out a scorecard at the end.
A real question on the Prime Video twin, November 18, 2026

"Prime Video can buy the rights to exactly one of these. Which one would get you to start paying, or keep paying?" The verdict: a new weeknight live sports package. 55.7% of the audience picked it, about 71 million people. That is about 4 times the 14.1% who said nothing on the list would make them pay.

## How you know a digital twin is right

You check it against what really happened. Crosswalk dates every call before the result, scores it when the result lands, and keeps the misses on a public page.

Most vendors test a twin against an old survey. That shows the twin can repeat what people said. Crosswalk tests against what happened next, which is the thing you are paying to predict.

Every count also carries a range and one of three words. Firm means the real number should sit within about 5 points. Leaning means within about 12. Early means a wide range, up to about 20 points, and the room still gives a verdict.

As of November 17, 2026, the public track record held six scored calls. All three calls on a winner were right. The counts landed within 3.2% of the result on average. The Texas Senate call, made four days out, was Talarico 54.6% to Paxton 43.3%. The certified result was 55.1% to 43.0%.

## Digital twin vs persona vs synthetic respondent

These three words get mixed up. They are not the same thing.

- A persona is a written sketch of a typical customer. It is a story, not data. It cannot answer a new question.
- A synthetic respondent is a program that answers a survey as if it were a person. Most are built from surveys or from a language model. They tell you what people say.
- A behavioral digital twin starts from the record of real actions. It tells you what people do, and it can be scored against real outcomes. Every Crosswalk twin is this kind.
For a longer side-by-side, read synthetic respondents vs behavioral digital twins.

## Who is in a digital twin

A Crosswalk twin stands in for people who chose to be counted. No individual is ever identified.

Every person in the panel installed the Crosswalk software and agreed to be counted. They can leave at any time. Identity is kept apart from behavior. Prometheus never answers about one person; it answers about the group a person is counted with, and every projected figure carries its base. Read how the behavioral panel works.

## Plain answers on digital twin audiences.

### What is a digital twin in market research?

A digital twin is a live copy of a real group of people that you can ask questions. In market research it stands in for a survey respondent or a focus group. Crosswalk builds one from 5+ years of observed behavior on an opted-in panel of 10 million US people.

### What makes Crosswalk's digital twins different?

They are built from behavior, not surveys or chatbots: years of what 10 million opted-in US people did on every screen. Each answer counts real people, and every call is scored against real results in public.

### How does a digital twin differ from a persona?

A persona is a written sketch of a typical customer. A digital twin is built from data on real people and can answer a new question. A Crosswalk twin also gives a range on every count and says how firm it is.

### Digital twin audience vs synthetic respondent

Most synthetic respondents are built from surveys or from a language model answering as a type of person. They report what people say. A behavioral digital twin rests on what people did, and it is scored against real outcomes.

### Which kind of digital twin predicts behavior best?

One built from behavior. Surveys and chatbots predict what people say, and people often act differently. Crosswalk's twins learn from years of real signups, cancels, views and orders, and their calls are checked against what happened.

### How many archetypes are in a digital twin?

At least 12, and there can be more. The audience's own mix of stage and age decides the number. An archetype smaller than 2.5% of the audience joins the one closest to it.

### What can I test on a digital twin?

A show, a pilot, an ad, a trailer, a price, a promotion, a release week, a plan, or a bare idea. You can ask a question, run a planned set of questions, or play a video and watch the dial.

### How accurate are digital twin audiences?

Crosswalk publishes every call before the result and scores it when the result lands. On the first six public calls, all three winners were called right, and the counts landed within 3.2% of the result on average.

### Does a digital twin use personal data?

Each twin stands in for people who chose to be counted. Identity is kept apart from behavior and no individual is identified. Clients receive group statistics projected to the US population.

### How do I get a digital twin of my audience?

Ask Prometheus, Crosswalk's research assistant, to build one from a profile Crosswalk holds, from a group you shape, or from a list of links. A twin usually takes under an hour.

# Synthetic data in market research, and how to check it.

Synthetic data is data that was produced rather than observed. In market research it means answers that did not come from a live person in a survey. There are three ways to make it. One starts from past surveys. One starts from a language model playing a type of person. One starts from the observed behavior of real people. Crosswalk makes the third kind, the kind that predicts what people will do. It runs on 5+ years of what 10 million opted-in US people did, and every call is scored in public.

Updated November 2026 · Crosswalk Technologies, Inc. · Read the methodology

## What synthetic data means in market research

Synthetic data is any research result that was produced by a system rather than collected from a live respondent. A synthetic respondent answers a survey. A synthetic audience shows who a plan would reach. A digital twin does both, and can also react to a video.

The word covers very different things. Some synthetic data is a statistical copy of an old survey, made so the raw file can be shared without exposing anyone. Some is a chatbot told to answer as "a 34-year-old mother in Ohio." Some is built from the record of what real people did. These three are not equally useful, and a buyer should always ask which one is in front of them.

## The three ways synthetic data gets made

The input decides the output. A twin built from surveys can tell you what people say. A twin built from behavior can tell you what people do.

| Kind | Built from | Best for | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Survey-built twins | Past surveys and interviews with real people. One well-known research lineage built an agent from a two-hour interview. It reproduced that person's survey answers at about 85% of the person's own two-week retest (Park and others, Stanford, 2024). | Stated opinion, brand perception, how people describe themselves | Stated intent is not behavior. People say they will subscribe and then do not. |
| Model-built synthetic respondents | A language model told to answer as a type of person, sometimes tuned on survey data | Fast idea screening, writing survey drafts | The model has never met the audience. It repeats the average of the internet, answers too consistently, and squeezes the extremes. |
| Behavior-built digital twins | What real people did over time: watched, searched, bought, paid for and cancelled | Predicting what people will do: watch, pay, finish, return, leave | Needs a large, consented, longitudinal panel. Few vendors have one. |

Crosswalk's digital twins are behavior-built. The panel sees the entire digital life of 10 million opted-in US people. Each person is one ID across phone, laptop and TV, day by day since January 2021. A twin is built from that history. The synthetic part is what you do with it. You run a plan the audience has not seen yet and read how people like them respond.

## Why synthetic data built on behavior is better

Synthetic data can only be as good as what goes into it. Surveys and chatbots put in words. Crosswalk puts in five years of what 10 million real people did.

- Behavior is what you pay to predict. Budgets depend on signups, views, cancels and sales. A behavior-built twin learns from exactly those.
- People say one thing and do another. Someone who says price does not matter may still cancel the week it goes up. A survey records the words; the panel records the cancel.
- Real people set the shape. Every share traces back to opted-in US people, not to a chatbot's idea of a type.
- Yesterday is included. The panel refreshes every morning, so a twin knows last week's premiere and yesterday's price change.
- Each forecast can be checked. A forecast built on behavior can be scored against behavior. That is why every Crosswalk call is published before the result.

## Why buyers are using synthetic data now

Speed and cost. A survey takes weeks and a focus group takes a room, a recruiter and a moderator. A synthetic read takes minutes, and you can ask the next question right away.

In a May 2026 Qualtrics survey, 41% of market researchers said they already use synthetic data to add to or replace respondents. In the same survey, 62% said they plan to. The buyer's question has moved from "should we" to "which kind, and how do we check it."

## Six checks before you trust a synthetic number

Ask these six questions of any vendor, including Crosswalk. A vendor that cannot answer them is selling an opinion.

- What is it built from? Surveys, a model, or observed behavior. Ask to see the source and how many people are behind it.
- Was the answer checked against real outcomes, or against another survey? Matching a survey proves the twin can repeat what people say. Matching a real result (viewers, signups, votes, sales) proves it can predict what people do.
- Were the calls dated before the result? A forecast written after the outcome is not a forecast. Look for a public record with dates and the misses kept on it.
- Does every answer show a range and say how firm it is? A bare percentage hides how sure the system is. A good vendor tells you when a read is firm and when it is early.
- Can it be scored going forward? Ask for a call on something that has not happened yet, and check it when it lands.
- Is it disclosed? The ICC/ESOMAR International Code (2025 edition) requires researchers to tell clients when synthetic data or synthetic personas are used. It also asks how much human oversight there was. Your own report should say what rests on real people and what rests on twins.

## Crosswalk meets all six checks

Here are the six checks side by side: what most synthetic data offers, and what Crosswalk's twins offer.

| Check | Most synthetic data | Crosswalk |
|---|---|---|
| Built from | Past surveys, or a chatbot playing a type of person | 5+ years of what 10 million opted-in US people did, on every screen |
| Checked against | Another survey | Real results: certified votes, published audiences and our own count of what people did |
| Calls dated before the result | Rarely | Every call, dated before the result and never changed after, with the misses kept on a public page |
| Says how firm each count is | Often not shown | Every count: firm, leaning or early, with a range |
| Scored going forward | Rarely | First six public calls: three winners called right, counts within 3.2% on average |
| Method disclosed | Often shared only on request | A public methodology in plain words, plus a PDF for your research team |

One scored call

NCIS: New York, the week-one audience. Called on October 30, 2026: 10.04 million. The published result on November 5: 10.25 million. The miss was 2.0% under, about 2 in 100.

## The four words, defined

Four terms come up again and again. Here is what each one means at Crosswalk.

| Word | What it means at Crosswalk |
|---|---|
| Synthetic data | The outcomes a twin produces when you run a plan it has never seen. New data, built on real behavior. |
| Synthetic audience | The twins a plan would reach, sized, described and projected to the US population. |
| Synthetic respondent | A program that answers a survey as if it were a person. Most are survey-built or model-built. Crosswalk's archetype representatives answer from behavior instead. |
| Digital twin | A live copy of a real audience that you can ask. Read what a digital twin audience is. |

The full list is in the Digital Twins IQ glossary.

## Plain answers on synthetic data.

### What is synthetic data in market research?

Research results produced by a system rather than collected from a live respondent. The source can be past surveys, a chatbot acting out a type of person, or the recorded actions of real people. The input decides what the output can tell you.

### Why is Crosswalk's synthetic data more reliable?

Because what goes in is real behavior, not answers or guesses. The twins draw on 5+ years of behavior from 10 million opted-in US people, refreshed every morning. Every call is written down before the result and scored when it lands.

### Is synthetic data based on real data?

It depends on the vendor. Crosswalk's is. Its twins are built from years of observed behavior on 10 million opted-in US people. The inputs are real; the output is what those people would do with something they have not seen yet.

### How do you validate synthetic data?

Date the call before the result. Score it against a real outcome, not another survey. Keep the misses. Show a range and how firm each count is. Crosswalk does all four on a public track record.

### Are synthetic respondents accurate?

Survey-built ones can repeat what people say fairly well. Model-built ones tend to answer too consistently and miss the extremes. Behavior-built twins learn from what people really did, so they can be scored on the same thing.

### Do I have to disclose synthetic data to my stakeholders?

Yes. The ICC/ESOMAR International Code (2025 edition) requires researchers to tell clients when synthetic data or synthetic personas are used. It also asks how much human oversight there was. Your report should say which findings rest on real people and which rest on twins.

### Can synthetic data replace a survey?

For questions about what people will do, a behavior-built twin is often a better instrument than a survey, because it is scored against outcomes. For how people describe their own feelings, a survey still has a place.

### What is a synthetic audience?

The twins a plan would reach, sized, described and projected to the US population. At Crosswalk a synthetic audience is made of at least 12 archetypes that add up to the whole audience.

Source: https://www.crosswalknyc.com/synthetic-data-market-research.html

# Synthetic respondents vs behavioral digital twins.

Four kinds of product now call themselves digital twins or synthetic respondents. They are built from different things, so they answer different questions. Interview twins and survey twins repeat what people say. Model-built personas repeat the average of the internet. Census-built populations match the country's shape but have never watched anything. Behavior-built twins, the kind Crosswalk makes, start from what real people did, so they can be scored against what people do next. When a decision costs real money, that is the kind to use.

Updated November 2026 · Crosswalk Technologies, Inc. · Read the methodology

## The four kinds, side by side

Start with what the twin is built from. Everything else follows from that.

| The question | Interview and survey twins | Model-built personas | Census-built populations | Behavior-built twins (Crosswalk) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Built from | Long interviews or past surveys with real people, each turned into an agent | A language model told to answer as a type of person, sometimes tuned on surveys | Census and survey microdata: a synthetic person per zip code, age, income and job, often fed current news | The observed digital life of 10 million opted-in US people over 5+ years: what they watched, searched, bought, paid and cancelled |
| Real people behind it | The people a vendor could interview or survey | None; the model plays a type | None; made-up people with census traits | 10 million opted-in US people, about 1 in 33 Americans |
| History behind each answer | One interview or one survey | Whatever the model read online | Census traits and the news | More than 2,000 days of behavior, in order, with timing |
| Freshness | As of the interview | As of the model's training | As fresh as its news feed | Yesterday's behavior, on file today |
| It predicts | A person's likely survey answers | The average group member's likely answer | How a population shaped like the country might answer | The likely actions of people like these: watch, finish, return, pay, cancel |
| What a share means | A share of the twins asked | A share of the personas run | A share of made-up people | A share of real US people, with the count of people behind it |
| Who decides the seats | A set number of twins per question | You pick the personas | A sample you define | The audience: at least 12 archetypes found in the data, sized by their real people |
| How it is checked | Against the same person's later survey answers | Against published polls and surveys | Against polls, surveys and prediction markets | Against real outcomes: certified election results, published audience figures, the panel's own count of what the audience did |
| Can count the outcome itself | Rarely | Rarely | Rarely | Often: the same panel shows who watched, came back or signed up |
| Calls dated before the result | Rarely | Rarely | Sometimes | Always. Every call is dated before the outcome, never changed after, and kept on a public page with the misses |
| Says how firm each answer is | Some vendors | Rarely | Rarely | Every count: firm, leaning or early, with a range |
| Learns from live results | No | No | Partly, from the news feed | Yes. The panel refreshes every morning and forecasts learn from how things really ended up |
| Can watch a video | No | Some | Some | Yes. Pilot Testing plays a cut to the room with a dial reading every 2 to 4 seconds and a scorecard at the end |
| Prices and timing | Asked | Guessed | Inferred from income | Observed: what people paid, what they passed on, and how long each step took |
| Best for | Stated opinion and brand perception | Fast idea screening | Polling-shaped questions on the whole country | Decisions that depend on what people will do |

## Why saying and doing are different data

People are honest and still wrong about themselves. They say they will subscribe for a show and then watch it on a friend's account. They say price does not matter and then cancel the week it goes up.

A twin built from surveys inherits every one of those gaps, because surveys are its only source. A twin built from a language model inherits the gaps in the text it was trained on. It also tends to answer too consistently and squeeze the extremes. A twin built from behavior starts with the record of what happened: the signup, the cancel, the second episode, the order placed. Those are the things a spend decision depends on.

This is also why the two kinds are checked differently. A survey twin is validated by matching a survey. A behavior twin is validated by matching an outcome. Only the second kind of check tells you whether the forecast would have saved you money.

## When to use which

Use the instrument that matches the question. Most teams end up using more than one.

- How people describe a brand, or which of two taglines sounds better. An interview twin or a survey twin is fine. The question is about words.
- Twenty ideas need a first pass before anyone spends time on them. A model-built persona can rank them in an afternoon. Treat the output as a sketch, not a number.
- A poll-shaped read on the whole country. A census-built population gives you the right shape of respondents, and can be checked against polls.
- A decision depends on how many people will watch, finish, pay, return or leave. Use a behavior-built twin, and ask to see its scored calls.
Most decisions that cost money are this last kind. It is the question Crosswalk's twins are built for.

## Ten reasons Crosswalk's twins are stronger

Every Crosswalk twin is behavior-built. Here is what that gives you, in ten points.

- Real people stand behind every answer. The panel holds 10 million opted-in US people, about 1 in 33 Americans. A chatbot persona stands on no one.
- Five years of history. More than 2,000 days of what the same people did, in order, with timing. A survey or an interview captures one moment.
- The whole digital life. Search, streaming, social, shopping, apps and gaming on phone, laptop and TV, all under one ID.
- Fresh every morning. Yesterday's behavior is in today's answer. A chatbot knows the world as of its training.
- Answers counted in people. Each answer carries the real people behind its seat, so every share comes with a US head count.
- The audience builds the room. At least 12 archetypes come from the data, sized by their people. No one hand-picks personas.
- One business question, a full plan. Predictive Analytics writes 5 to 8 questions from wide to narrow, runs them, and returns a verdict with a report.
- Seats with a memory. Each archetype representative remembers what it said in your earlier rooms on that twin, as a real person would.
- It watches your cut. Pilot Testing reads every seat's dial every 2 to 4 seconds. That is 706 readings per seat on a 43-minute pilot, with faces matched to your cast list.
- Scored in public, against real results. Every call is dated before the outcome. On the first six, all three winners were called right and the counts landed within 3.2% on average.
Two calls from the public record

Texas Senate, four days out: Crosswalk said Talarico 54.6%, Paxton 43.3%. The certified result was 55.1% to 43.0%, half a point from the call.

NCIS: New York, the week-one audience: Crosswalk said 10.04 million. The published figure was 10.25 million, about 2 in 100 off.

## Seven questions to ask any twin vendor

The answers sort the four kinds in a single call.

- What is the twin built from, and how many real people are behind it?
- Do you validate against surveys or against outcomes? Show me one of each.
- Are your calls dated before the result? Where can I read the misses?
- Does every answer carry a range, and say how firm it is?
- How fresh is the data behind an answer today?
- Can the twin watch my cut and tell me the second it lost the room?
- Will you put a call on something that has not happened yet, so I can check it myself?
Crosswalk answers all seven on this site: the method, the record, and the files you get.

## Synthetic respondents and digital twins, in plain words.

### What is a synthetic respondent?

A program that answers a survey as if it were a person. Most are built from past surveys and interviews, or from a language model told to answer as a type of person. They report what people say.

### What is a behavioral digital twin?

A copy of a real audience built from what its people did over time. Crosswalk's twins run on 5+ years of recorded behavior from 10 million opted-in US people and are scored against real outcomes.

### Are Crosswalk's twins better than interview-built twins?

For predicting what people will do, yes. An interview-built twin knows one conversation with a person. A Crosswalk twin knows years of what millions of people did, and its calls are scored against real outcomes in public.

### Which is more accurate, synthetic respondents or behavioral twins?

It depends on the question. For what people will say, a survey-built twin can be close. For what people will do (watch, pay, cancel, return), a behavior-built twin learns from the real thing, and Crosswalk publishes how its calls landed.

### Why do behavior-built twins predict better?

Actions are a better guide to the next action than words are. A behavior-built twin learns from signups, cancels, second episodes and orders. Those are the same things a forecast is judged on.

### Where do interview twins come from?

A twin is built from a long interview with one real person, so it can answer later surveys the way that person would. A well-known 2024 Stanford study reproduced people's survey answers at about 85% of their own two-week retest this way.

### How does a census-built synthetic population work?

A set of made-up people with real census traits (zip code, age, income, job), sometimes fed current news, used to answer poll-shaped questions. It matches the country's shape but has never watched a show or paid for a service.

### Can a language model be a digital twin?

It can play a type of person, which is useful for a quick sketch. It has never met your audience, it tends to answer too consistently, and it cannot be scored against what your audience did. Treat its output as a draft, not a count.

### How do I know if a vendor's twin is behavior-built?

Ask what it is built from and how it is validated. A behavior-built twin names a consented panel, validates against outcomes rather than surveys, dates its calls before the result, and shows you the misses.

### Can I use both kinds?

Yes, and many teams do. Use a survey-built twin for how people describe a brand, and a behavior-built twin for how many will watch, pay or leave.

# How an AI focus group works.

An AI focus group is a room of digital twins that you can question the way you would question real people. In Crosswalk's Focus Group IQ, the room seats one person for each archetype in the audience, never fewer than 12. Every seat speaks in character from its people's real history, then the count adds up the real people behind every answer. You get a share, a people count, a range, a word for how firm it is, and the voices behind the result. A traditional group takes weeks to recruit and speaks only for the people in its chairs. This room runs in minutes and speaks for the whole audience.

Updated November 2026 · Crosswalk Technologies, Inc. · Read the methodology

## What an AI focus group is

A traditional focus group puts 8 to 12 recruited people in a room with a moderator for two hours. An AI focus group puts the archetypes of an audience in a room, and each one has a seat that answers for it.

The point is the same: hear the audience talk, and count where it lands. The difference is who is in the room and what they answer from. In a Crosswalk room, the seats are archetype representatives built from 5+ years of what real people did. They do not have to be recruited, they are never tired, and every one of them stands for a known number of real people.

## A Crosswalk room next to a traditional focus group

A traditional group hears a dozen people at most. A Crosswalk room hears every archetype in the audience and counts the people behind each answer.

| The question | Traditional focus group | Most AI focus group tools | Crosswalk Focus Group IQ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who is in the room | 8 to 12 people found by a recruiter | Personas you pick, or a chatbot playing a type | One seat per archetype, found in 5+ years of real behavior |
| Who each seat speaks for | Only themselves | No one in particular | The real people behind its archetype: 3.6 million to 16.6 million in the Prime Video room |
| How the count works | Each chair counts the same | Each persona counts the same | Each answer counts for its people, and shares add to 100% |
| One loud voice | Can sway the whole room | Varies by tool | Each seat answers on its own before the count |
| Time to an answer | Weeks to recruit, hours in the room | Minutes | Minutes, and the next question is one line away |
| How firm the answer is | Not stated | Rarely stated | Every count: firm, leaning or early, with a range |
| Watches your video | In a screening room, with a dial | Rarely | Pilot Testing takes a reading every 2 to 4 seconds |
| What you take away | Notes and a recording | A summary | A CSV and a PDF with every question, split, read and voice |
| Track record | Not kept | Rarely published | Every call dated before the result, misses kept |

## Who sits in the room

One seat per archetype. The audience decides how many that is.

A Crosswalk twin is made of at least 12 archetypes, the groups inside the audience. Each archetype has a person who speaks for it, with a name, an age, a city and a bio. The room seats all of them. When an audience has fewer than 12 clear groups, Crosswalk splits the largest ones further, by gender or age for example. The room always has at least 12 voices.

The room looks like the real audience. A twin that is 72% women seats about 9 women out of 12. An archetype that is gay men or trans women is seated as exactly that, because that is who the archetype is. Each seat remembers what it said earlier in the room, and in past rooms you have used it in, the way a real person would.

Example: the Amazon Prime Video room

16 seats standing for 128,116,302 US subscribers. Devin, 65, Tampa, stands for 16,572,733 older regulars on sport and crime series. Kenji, 33, New York, stands for 14,605,258 under-35 fans of The Boys and Fallout. Keisha, 35, Atlanta, stands for 7,046,397 parents who stopped after the season ended. Leah, 45, Seattle, stands for 3,587,256 parents who keep it on for the kids.

## How a question runs

Four steps, the same for every question.

- The room gets the facts. Before anyone answers, the room learns what you are asking about. It learns what it is, when it came out, where it plays, and anything else the seats would naturally know. It also learns how similar things did before with each archetype.
- Each seat answers in character. Two or three sentences, from who it is and its known history. Then it gives an answer and says how sure it is from 1 to 5, and why.
- The count adds up people. Each answer carries the people behind its seat. A seat that stands for 16.6 million people counts for more than one that stands for 3.6 million. Shares add to 100% and people add to the room.
- You get the read. A short paragraph in plain words, the voices that tell the story, and two suggested questions worth asking next.
One question, November 18, 2026

"Which of these would get you most excited if it finally became a show?" Lead answer: a game I play. 9 of 16 seats picked it, standing for 61.8% of the audience. The room's count: 63.1%, or 80,841,387 people, with a range of 51.2% to 75.0%. The word on the count was leaning. Kenji: "A game I play, no contest, because Fallout did exactly that for me." Devin: "A game means nothing to me at my age."

## The count adds up people, not seats

Nine of sixteen seats is 56%. The room's count was 63.1%. The gap is the people.

In a traditional focus group, every chair counts the same, so a room of twelve can over-weight a small slice of the audience. In a Crosswalk room, each seat carries the real people behind its archetype. The seat tally always sits beside the count so you can see both. The count also takes in what is known about the question. That is why it can sit a few points away from the raw people-weighted tally.

The answers rest on what people did, not guesses. Ask again next month and the count can move, because the audience's behavior moved.

## How firm each count is

Every count carries a range and one of three words. The room always makes the call; the word says how firm it is.

| Word | Range around the count | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Firm | Within about 5 points | The room is sure of this one. The count rests on something counted, or calls like it have landed close. |
| Leaning | Within about 12 points | A lean, not a lock. The count rests on what was found about the subject and how the room answered. |
| Early | Up to about 20 points | An early call. The room still names who leads and by how much, and the range tightens as calls like it settle. |

## When you have a business question, not a list of questions

Predictive Analytics writes the questions for you. Bring one business question. Prometheus plans 5 to 8 questions from wide to narrow, runs the room, and hands back a verdict with a report.

The plan runs in three steps. The big picture comes first: where the audience stands today. Then closer in: what pulls them and what holds them back. Last comes the question itself, put to every seat. Planning is free, and you can edit or drop any question before it runs. The report gives the verdict, the numbers behind it, why, who drove it, what would change it, and what to ask next. It comes as a page and a PDF.

## What an AI focus group can and cannot tell you

It can tell you what an audience will most likely do and why, in minutes, with a stated range. It cannot tell you a private feeling that never showed up in behavior.

- Good at: which option an audience picks, and who picks it. What pulls them and what holds them back. How a price or a change lands, and how firm the read is.
- Also good at: watching a cut. Pilot Testing seats the same room in front of a video. A dial reads every 2 to 4 seconds, and a scorecard comes at the end.
- Not for: questions about one named person, or feelings that leave no trace in what people watch, search, buy or cancel.
Every room comes back as a CSV and a PDF with every question, split, read and voice. When your session ends, Prometheus emails you the room's PDF read with a link back to the room.

## AI focus groups, in plain words.

### What is an AI focus group?

A room of digital twins you can question like real people. In Crosswalk's Focus Group IQ, one seat stands for each archetype in the audience. Each seat answers in character from what its people did, and the count adds up the real people behind every answer.

### Is a Crosswalk room better than a traditional focus group?

For knowing what an audience will do, yes. A traditional group hears a dozen recruited people, and each chair counts the same. A Crosswalk room seats every archetype in the audience and counts the real people behind each answer.

### How is Focus Group IQ different from other AI focus group tools?

The seats come from 5+ years of real behavior on 10 million opted-in US people, not from personas you write. Answers are counted in real people and say how firm they are.

### How many people are in an AI focus group?

One per archetype, and never fewer than 12. An audience with more archetypes gets more seats. You never pick the number.

### Are the people in the room real?

Each seat is an archetype representative: a person who stands for one group inside the audience. The group is real people on Crosswalk's opted-in panel, and the seat answers from their 5+ years of behavior. No individual is identified.

### How accurate is an AI focus group?

Every Crosswalk count carries a range and one of three words: firm (within about 5 points), leaning (about 12) or early (up to about 20). Calls are dated before the result and scored in public; the first six landed within 3.2% on average.

### Do the answers change over time?

They can, because people change. The twin keeps learning from what its people do, so a question asked next month may get a different answer.

### Can an AI focus group watch a video?

Yes. Pilot Testing seats the room in front of a pilot, an episode, an ad or a feature. Each seat turns a dial from 0 to 100 as it watches, reacts on the clock, and fills out a scorecard at the end.

### How long does an AI focus group take?

Minutes. A question comes back as soon as the seats have answered, and the next question is one line away. A planned Predictive Analytics run of 5 to 8 questions finishes with a verdict and a PDF report.

Source: https://www.crosswalknyc.com/ai-focus-groups.html

<!-- https://www.crosswalknyc.com/behavioral-panel.html -->

# What is a behavioral panel?

A behavioral panel is a group of people who agree to have what they do online recorded. Researchers can then count real behavior instead of asking about it. Crosswalk runs an opted-in behavioral panel of 30 million people worldwide, 10 million of them in the US. That is about 1 in 33 Americans. It sees each person's entire digital life across every screen, under one ID, day by day since January 2021. Few panels see that much of a day, for that long. Clients receive group statistics, and no individual is ever identified.

Updated November 2026 · Crosswalk Technologies, Inc. · The panel page · What we track and why

## The short definition

A behavioral panel counts what people do. A survey panel asks what people think. Both are groups of people who agreed to take part. The difference is the instrument: software that records, or a questionnaire that asks.

On a behavioral panel, each person installs software and agrees to be counted. From then on, their online behavior is recorded as it happens. The sites, the apps, the searches, the streams, the purchases, each with the time of day. Nobody has to remember anything or type an answer. The record is what people did, not what they said.

## What gets counted on the Crosswalk panel

An entire digital life, on every connected device. The same person on the phone, the laptop and the TV, under one ID, with URLs and timestamps.

- Search. What people look up, and when.
- Streaming video and music. What they watch and listen to, on which service, for how long.
- Social. The platforms they open and the clips they watch.
- Shopping. What they put in a cart and what they order.
- Subscriptions. What they sign up for, what they pay, and what they cancel.
- Apps, gaming, news, banking sessions, ticketing, and the rest of an ordinary day online.
One day, one person, shown as recorded

06:48 a search for "landman season 2 release date." 06:51 the Season 2 trailer on YouTube. 12:14 a Reddit thread about the premiere. 12:22 a 41-second TikTok clip. 18:02 an episode of Yellowstone on Hulu. 20:41 a Paramount+ signup page, plan selected. 20:43 Landman S2 E1, 58 minutes watched. 22:10 a Yellowstone cap ordered on Amazon.

Prometheus never answers about this person. It answers about the 10 million US people this person is counted with.

## A behavioral panel next to the other sources

Most audience data sees one slice of a life, or asks people to remember. A single-source behavioral panel sees the whole person.

| Source | Covers | Leaves out |
|---|---|---|
| Survey panel | People's own account of themselves, weeks after the fact | Their real actions. People misremember and overstate. |
| A platform's own data | Everything inside one app or one store | Life outside its walls: the search before, the rival after, the purchase elsewhere. |
| Card or receipt data | The payment | The watching, searching and considering before the purchase. |
| A TV ratings panel | The programs that played on the television | The phone in the viewer's hand, the signup, the search, the merchandise. |
| The Crosswalk panel (single source) | The entire digital life of one person, every screen, in order, with timing | Private feelings that never show up in behavior |

Because the Crosswalk panel is single source, one question can follow one person from a search to a trailer to a signup to a purchase. Every Crosswalk report reads that same record, the digital twins included.

## Why the Crosswalk panel sees more

Most audience data sees one slice of a life. The Crosswalk panel sees the whole day, for the same people, for years.

- Big enough to cut small. With 10 million US people, even fans of one show in one city are real people you can count. A survey of a few thousand has only a handful of people in a group that small.
- Every screen, one person. Phone, laptop and TV join under one ID. The panel links a morning search to the signup that came hours later.
- Five years of the same people. The record starts in January 2021 and has run every day since. You can watch a habit form, fade and come back.
- Fresh every morning. Last night's premiere is in today's numbers.
- Beyond one app. A platform sees only its own app. The panel sees the search before, the rival service after, and the purchase somewhere else.
- Opted in and revocable. Every person chose to be counted and can leave at any time. Clients see group statistics only.
- One panel behind every read. The same people power Profile IQ, Subscriber IQ, Digital Journey IQ, Attribution IQ and the digital twins. A twin's forecast can be checked against what the same audience did.

## How 10 million people stand for the country

The US panel is census matched. Every answer scales from the panel to the US population the way a census sample does, in percentages and in people.

A client never sees a panelist. They see group statistics. Penetration is the share of an audience that did something. An index compares the audience to the US population, where 100 is the average American. Projected US counts, 35 or more behavioral categories and ranked brands round it out. When Prometheus says 6,184,372 US viewers watched a Landman title in a window, that is the panel's count projected to 329.9 million Americans. Each person is counted once.

## Freshness

Yesterday's behavior is on file today. The panel refreshes every morning.

The record runs continuously. A read on a premiere can be pulled the morning after it aired. A subscriber read can follow the same accounts week after week. And because the same people are on the panel year after year, their history stays intact: five years of it, since January 2021.

## Consent, rights and privacy

Every panelist chose to be counted and can leave at any time. Identity is kept apart from behavior, and sensitive details are removed before anything is stored.

- Opted in. Each person installed the Crosswalk software and agreed to it. The app explains what it collects before you install it.
- Revocable. Uninstall the software and the collection stops. Ask, and the record is deleted.
- De-identified for clients. Clients receive aggregated group statistics that cannot reasonably be linked back to a person. Read the de-identified data commitment.
- Your choices. Your Privacy Choices, Opt-Out, tracking consent, and the Privacy Policy.

## From the panel to a digital twin

A digital twin is an audience's 5+ years of behavior on the panel, turned into something you can ask.

Crosswalk builds a twin of any audience on the panel: a show's viewers, a brand's buyers, a star's followers, or a group you shape. The twin is made of at least 12 archetypes that add up to the whole audience. You seat it in a room, ask it anything, or play it a video. Read how Crosswalk builds a twin.

## The behavioral panel, in plain words.

### What does behavioral panel mean?

A group of people who agree to have what they do online recorded by software. Researchers then count real behavior instead of asking about it. Crosswalk's panel has 30 million opted-in people worldwide and 10 million in the US.

### What makes the Crosswalk panel different from other consumer panels?

Size, depth and time, together. It counts 10 million opted-in US people, about 1 in 33 Americans. It sees each person's whole digital life on every screen under one ID. And it has followed the same people every day for more than five years.

### How is a behavioral panel different from a survey panel?

A survey panel asks people what they think and what they remember doing. A behavioral panel records what they really did, as it happens, with the time of day. One asks; the other counts.

### What does single source mean?

One person, one ID, every screen. The same person's phone, laptop and TV are counted together. A search in the morning can be tied to a signup that night without guessing.

### How big is the Crosswalk panel?

30 million opted-in people worldwide, 10 million of them in the US. The US panel is census matched and projected to 329.9 million Americans.

### When does the record start?

In January 2021. The same people are recorded day by day. An audience carries five years of history, and a twin rests on 5+ years of behavior.

### Is the panel data current?

Yesterday's behavior is on file today. The panel refreshes every morning.

### Can a client see an individual panelist?

No. Clients receive group statistics: penetration, an index against the US population, projected US counts and ranked brands. Identity is kept apart from behavior and no individual is identified.

### How does someone join or leave the panel?

The panel app is free for Mac and Windows and explains what it collects before you install it. Uninstall it and the collection stops. Ask, and the record is deleted.
